teaching.hint: Could it be easier to identify which cells must survive than to test every enclosed region?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The surviving O cells are exactly those reachable from any boundary O through O-only side connections.
solution_outline.approach: Traverse from all boundary O cells and mark reached cells temporarily. Then capture unmarked O cells and restore the marked cells to O. An explicit frontier avoids recursion-depth dependence.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Temporarily marked cells are exactly the O cells already reached from the boundary; original X cells are never used as traversal links.
solution_outline.correctness: Every marked cell follows an O path from an edge, so its region must survive. Every O region meeting an edge is fully reached by traversal; an interior-only component cannot be reached from another component. Thus the final sweep preserves exactly the edge-connected regions and captures exactly all others.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(m*n)` time and `O(m*n)` auxiliary frontier space in the worst case, while changing the original board.
solution_outline.pitfall: Checking only whether an individual cell is interior misses long corridors connecting its region to an edge.

source_fidelity_notes: Restated enclosure as exact connected-component edge membership without diagrams; retained in-place mutation and side-only connections.
Added the single-row example to make boundary semantics observable without revealing a traversal method.
common_wrong_turns: Checking only whether an individual cell is interior misses long corridors connecting its region to an edge.
